speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms first started relative to your birth?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your older brother had pyloric stenosis, which typically presents after a few weeks of life, and your symptoms started immediately with bilious vomiting, this points toward a different obstruction. Have you noticed any abdominal distension or a visible "olive-shaped" mass upon palpation?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia. The presentation of bilious vomiting within the first 24 hours of life, absence of an olive-shaped mass, and a family history of gastric outlet obstruction (which can sometimes coexist or be confused) strongly suggests a proximal small bowel obstruction. Given the immediate onset and bilious nature, duodenal atresia is the most likely diagnosis.
